builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: AutoAssumption: Searching over Assumptions Discovers ML-Systems Algorithms
summary: AutoAssumption replaces manual or program-level algorithm search (as in AlphaEvolve/OpenEvolve) with LLM search over explicit assumptions in Lean-checked proof graphs, relaxing one assumption of a published method, re-deriving it, and generating code. It costs the effort of formalizing target algorithms as Lean proof graphs plus LLM search and verification compute, which is a substantial per-domain upfront investment beyond typical inference-engineering workflows. It can fail because a verified proof does not guarantee the generated code is efficient or correct in deployment, the reported gains are specific to the evaluated benchmarks and models, and domains not yet formalized cannot be searched.
rationale: The discovered eviction and pruning algorithms are relevant to constrained-infrastructure inference, but adopting the harness itself requires Lean formalization effort and workload-specific validation of whether its gains transfer to the reader's models and serving stack.
technique: Assumption-relaxation search over Lean proof graphs

claims.statement: AutoAssumption replaces manual or program-level algorithm search (as in AlphaEvolve/OpenEvolve) with LLM search over explicit assumptions in Lean-checked proof graphs, relaxing one assumption of a published method, re-deriving it, and generating code. It costs the effort of formalizing target algorithms as Lean proof graphs plus LLM search and verification compute, which is a substantial per-domain upfront investment beyond typical inference-engineering workflows. It can fail because a verified proof does not guarantee the generated code is efficient or correct in deployment, the reported gains are specific to the evaluated benchmarks and models, and domains not yet formalized cannot be searched.

The discovered KV-cache eviction algorithm achieved the highest RULER-4K score among published methods run, the pruning algorithm achieved the lowest perplexity of thirteen methods on four LLaMA models, and at equal budget the harness scored within one point of OpenEvolve with lower variance across repeats.
